name: Kesed
title: Nahor's son
summary: Kesed was one of the eight sons of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his wife Milcah. He is mentioned in the genealogy in Genesis 22. Kesed is traditionally regarded as the ancestor of the Chaldeans (kasdim in Hebrew), the people who later founded the Neo-Babylonian Empire.

keyEvents.title: Birth of Kesed mentioned
keyEvents.description: After Abraham's binding of Isaac, Abraham is told that his brother Nahor has had eight sons with his wife Milcah, including Kesed.

keyEvents.title: Abraham's lineage
keyEvents.description: Kesed was the nephew of Abraham, the patriarch. Through this family line, Abraham's family is connected to the peoples of Mesopotamia.

keyEvents.title: Connection to the Chaldeans
keyEvents.description: The name Kesed (Hebrew: כֶּשֶׂד) is traditionally linked to the Chaldeans (kasdim), the people from Ur in Chaldea, which was Abraham's original homeland.

keyEvents.title: Nahor's lineage
keyEvents.description: Nahor's sons, including Kesed, represent various ethnic groups in the ancient Middle East, and this family line shows the spread of Abraham's extended family.
